world_news.headline: David Jones’ total debt is over $400m including millions owed to staff, administrators confirm
world_news.summary:
Creditors meeting hears upmarket retailer owes $11m to employees and recorded a net loss of $228m last financial year

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Upmarket retailer David Jones collapsed into administration earlier this month owing well over $400m, after accelerating financial losses and reputational damage threatened its ability to stock shelves for Christmas.

About 500 creditors attended its first meeting on Tuesday, where administrators McGrathNicol broke down the 188-year-old chain’s massive debt pile, including an estimated $180m owed to suppliers and $11m to employees.

world_news.headline: Rio Tinto agrees to pay US$250m to begin repairing ‘devastation’ left by Panguna mine
world_news.summary:
Community leader says fund gives chance to find solutions to ‘huge problems we have been living with since the days of the mine’s operation’

Anglo-Australian miner Rio Tinto has agreed to pay a quarter-of-a-billion dollars to begin the clean-up of the toxic Panguna mine site it abandoned more than three decades ago.

Panguna, once one of the world’s most profitable gold and copper mines, was shuttered in 1989 after violent protests over environmental damage and the inequitable division of the mine’s profits sparked a decade-long civil war on the Papua New Guinean island of Bougainville.

world_news.headline: Truck driver fired for ‘unsafe’ use of smartglasses in first reported sacking over device in Australia
world_news.summary:
Toll employee Ricardo Martins Silva used smartglasses to take photos at an LPG terminal despite the risk of an explosion caused by an electrical spark, a court heard

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A Toll truck driver was fired from work in Victoria after using smartglasses to snap photos at an LPG terminal, in what was described as an “intrinsically unsafe” incident.

It is the first reported case in Australia of a worker dismissed for using smartglasses in a workplace.

world_news.headline: Five EU states announce plans for immigration ‘return hubs’ in Rwanda
world_news.summary:
Germany, Austria, Netherlands, Denmark and Greece likely to face challenges to policy criticised as ‘grave moral failing’

Five EU member states have announced plans to set up an offshore centre in Rwanda for people with no legal right to stay in Europe, in a pilot scheme that is expected to face legal challenges and has been denounced as “a grave moral failing”.

The five countries – Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, Denmark and Greece – are the first to seek to use the EU’s newly agreed returns law that allows people who have exhausted all avenues of appeal against their removal from Europe to be sent to a third country.
